doc.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

chapter: Condon's circle and New York scene
title: Learning tunes and the first fake book
summary: Building repertoire after being caught not knowing tunes, helped by an illegal fake book.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: What would happen on a gig like that if someone called a tune and you didn’t know it?

I had several experiences with that. In the beginning I felt hesitant about saying I didn’t know a song I thought I can get by with it. And a lot of them you could. You could kind of fake and figure out. But once in a while you’d get one where and it would be some strange changes in it. And it would be embarrassing. I was very embarrassed about that and I decided I’ve got to learn these songs. So I started to increase my repertoire, to keep a little step ahead of all these guys so before they called them out I’d know them. So it’s rarely that I get stuck, but still today, even today, somebody will call something, but now I don’t feel funny about saying hey, wait, no.
I guess I’m curious because there wasn’t jazz books like today, so did you just like keep your ears open and say oh I hear someone playing this tune and I don’t know it, I’d better learn that one.
Well there was a fake book that did come out around the 40s. It was the first fake book. I still have it.
I still have it at home, God the thing is falling apart. But it was illegal to have it. Because these people, the songwriters were getting no royalties out of this. So it was a legal thing.

I paid twenty bucks for it then. And I treasured it. And all the tunes were in it. And so I got to learn a lot of songs through this book. If I heard a song being played that I didn’t know I’d go home and learn it. So I’d try to learn two or three songs a week and after a year or two I had a pretty good repertoire. I was in pretty good shape at that point.
